output_list.reason: The mintToken function has an integer overflow vulnerability. It allows the owner to set the balance of an arbitrary user to any value. This can be exploited to achieve a denial of service attack or to grant arbitrary additional units of the token to a user.
The transferFrom function does not check if the spender is a contract allowing it to execute arbitrary code. This can be exploited to allow unauthorized transactions from a user's account.
The approve function has an integer overflow vulnerability. It allows the owner to set the allowance to a very high value, if the allowance is a uint8, it can overflow and set it to 0.

The burn function has an integer overflow vulnerability. It allows the owner to burn arbitrary amount of tokens from a user's balance, causing an integer underflow and a potentially exploitable vulnerability.

output_list.vulnerability: The burnFrom function has an integer overflow vulnerability. It allows the owner to burn arbitrary amount of tokens from a user's balance, causing an integer underflow and a potentially exploitable vulnerability.
